text:
Laura: seeing a p99 jump on hosted today around 08:23 UTC, looks like 4x baseline for ~8m. p50 mostly fine.
Mike: any obvious deploys or config changes?
perf-bot: alert: hosted/p99_latency > 1200ms for 8m (link: https://grafana.redwood/hosted/p99). top affected route: /v1/generate.
Ines: grabbing runtime logs now. initial glance: repeated kernel selection events at high frequency on the same workers. suspected churn when seq_len distribution shifts.
Vijay: KV cache eviction metric spiked at same time: kvcache.evictions_per_min ~ 7x. Could be prefetch + eviction interaction.
Sam: rate-limiter also shows a short burst from tenant T-451 at 08:22:50, sustained ~30s; not huge QPS but lots of medium-length requests (~800-1800 tokens).
Laura: hm medium-long requests + burst could shift kernel choice to larger-matmul kernels -> slower per-token path + cache thrash.
Mike: can you paste the kernel switch logs?
Ines: paste: ```
[08:22:51] worker-17 kernel_select: seq_len=512 -> kernel=matmul_q4a_512 (fast)
[08:22:52] worker-17 kernel_select: seq_len=1500 -> kernel=matmul_q4a_2048 (slow_path)
[08:22:53] worker-17 kvcache: evict key=tenant:T-451:pref_abc size=2.3MB
[08:22:53] worker-17 kernel_select: seq_len=600 -> kernel=matmul_q4a_512
[08:22:54] worker-17 kvcache: miss key=tenant:T-451:pref_abc
[08:22:54] worker-17 kernel_select: seq_len=1700 -> kernel=matmul_q4a_2048
```
Mike: those rapid flips every sec would break batching heuristics and increase queue depth while the runtime swaps kernels.
Laura: queue depth graph shows micro-spikes aligned with kernel switch cadence. p95 latency climbs during each flip window.
Vijay: I also see the prefetch probe task ramped up around the same time (prefetch.probe_rate +3x) due to an internal heuristic that tries to warm KV keys for this tenant. Prefetch + eviction loop looks likely.
Sam: Tenant T-451 is running a large chat session with long context expansion (LLM agent). Could be chat client hitting many nested tool calls.
Ines: profiling snapshot attached: CPU samples show 40% in matmul kernel A (large) vs usual 12%. Memory bandwidth also up.
Laura: proposed mitigations: 1) throttle prefetch for tenants flagged as noisy, 2) temporarily pin kernel affinity to favor the fast_small kernel for workers serving hosted, 3) add short cooldown on kernel selection (e.g., 3s) to avoid churn. Which is quick to roll?
Mike: #2 can be done via runtime flag per pool: `--force-kernel-affinity=fast_small` config, can deploy to a subset (canary) in ~10m. #1 requires changing prefetch policy and quick config push, also ~15-30m to test. #3 code change, needs review, not immediate.
Vijay: quick patch: reduce prefetch.probe_rate for tenant T-451 via admin API: `POST /admin/tenants/T-451/config {"prefetch": {"probe_rate": 0.1}}` -> immediate effect.
Laura: do it. Also roll out kernel-affinity to one hosted pool and monitor p99.
Sam: applied rate change at 08:24:05. prefetched probe rate dropped, kvcache.evictions back down within 30s.
perf-bot: metric update: hosted/p99 down from 1300ms -> 420ms after mitigation window (08:24:40).
Mike: started canary with `--force-kernel-affinity=fast_small` on pool hosted-us-west-2-a at 08:26. Observing latency tail now 300-600ms, stable.
Ines: re-run reproduction harness locally to verify: command: ```
./tools/stress_client --tenant=T-451 --seq-dist="mix:20:1500,80:512" --qps=12 --duration=120
```
Ines: reproduction shows same kernel-flip behavior if we enable aggressive prefetch + no affinity. With affinity pinned flips stop and KV miss rate drops.
Laura: action items: 1) keep tenant prefetch throttled (Sam) 2) keep canary kernel-affinity for 1h then decide (Mike) 3) add cooldown to kernel selector and add a smoothing step in batching heuristics to resist 1s-level seq_len jitter (Ines) 4) write RCA note (Laura).
Sam: I added tenant tag noisy=true in admin so we can auto-apply throttles if eviction spikes.
Vijay: add a metric alert for kernel_switch_rate > 5/min per worker, that'll catch fast churn.
Laura: thanks all. I'll draft the incident blurb and update postmortem later.
Mike: tentative commit for affinity flag rollout at 08:35; will update thread. :thumbsup:
